Subject: Intermittent large-packet drops across on-prem GRE (MTU + NAT + SG overlap)

Hi Sam / AstraClad networking team,

We saw recurring packet drops when customers upload large artifacts across the private GRE link this morning. Symptoms: TCP sessions (large transfers) stall after ~1.5MB transferred, retransmit storms appear, and we see lots of ICMP fragmentation-needed messages on the on-prem gateway. The impacted path terminates at AstraClad's firewall before transiting your edge to our GRE.

What we've gathered so far (attachments included):
- pcap_fragmented_tcp.pcap: shows TCP segments getting fragmented and then dropped upstream.
- config-diff.txt: small diff of our GRE interface MTU (+ we rolled out a conntrack tweak last night).
- Observed conntrack table growth on the gateway coincident with the transfer windows (likely ephemeral port exhaustion).

Quick ask: Can you confirm whether any firewall/edge changes were deployed around 08:00 PDT? Also please share the ASA/NGFW MTU settings and whether there are any SNAT devices that could be clamping/rewriting DF bits.

We're standing by to join a live troubleshooting call; tagging Vanessa to coordinate.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Intermittent large-packet drops across on-prem GRE (MTU + NAT + SG overlap)

Thanks Monica — I started a packet capture on our egress GRE endpoint and pushed a short tcpdump to the shared Drive link (see NET-2024). Initial observations match: DF=1 for the large segments and an ICMP need-to-fragment from AstraClad's edge.

Immediate suggestions while we triage:
- Can AstraClad confirm the path MTU across their NGFW -> transit -> border? If any device is doing DF clearing or silently dropping fragments we need that callout.
- We will temporarily clamp MSS on the GRE endpoint to 1400 as a test; that should prevent fragmentation while we identify root cause.
- Karthik, can you run a conntrack histogram on the gateway VM and grep for high ephemeral reuse? I suspect SNAT entropy exhaustion combined with long-lived uploads.

If AstraClad can share firewall logs for the time window (08:00–09:30 PDT) that would help. I'm free for an ad-hoc call in 30 mins.

— Vanessa
Network Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Intermittent large-packet drops across on-prem GRE (MTU + NAT + SG overlap)

Hi all — we did deploy a micro-upgrade to the perimeter NGFW around 08:05 PDT (minor kernel/packet path patch). No intentional MTU changes were made. Early log checks show a handful of ICMP frag-needed with source IPs from your GRE peer and dst our border. We also see state table growth on our firewall during the same window.

We're spinning up a debug capture and will look for asymmetric routing (packets out one path, return on another) and any DF bit clears. I'll post the capture and our firewall syslog excerpt to networking_ops@astraclad.com in ~20 minutes.

Karthik — can you focus on:

- whether our SNAT implementation rewrites DF/DF handling when mapping ephemeral ports

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sam Li <sam.li@astraclad.com>, networking_ops@astraclad.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-packet drops across on-prem GRE (MTU + NAT + SG overlap)

TL;DR — root cause: a combination of (1) AstraClad NGFW micro-upgrade changed packet reassembly behavior (started sending frag-needed instead of accepting fragments), (2) our gateway NIC had GSO enabled and was handing large segments to the NIC which then dropped packets when DF was set, and (3) conntrack max default was lowered during last week's maintenance which caused faster ephemeral port churn under heavy parallel uploads.

Actions taken (completed):
- Disabled GSO on the gateway NICs (ethtool -K eth0 gso off) to ensure kernel-level segmentation and correct DF handling.
- Applied MSS clamp 1400 on GRE interface for ingress from AstraClad (temporary test) — uploads stabilized in the next measurement window.
- Increased conntrack_max to 524288 and adjusted tcp timeout to 600s on gateway; this prevented ephemeral exhaustion during large transfer bursts.
- Confirmed with Sam that NGFW will roll back the micro-upgrade to validate difference; they have a patch candidate to fix reassembly behavior.

Follow-ups / playbook updates:
- I uploaded a short remediation playbook into the shared Drive: playbook_mtu_remediation.md (contains commands, validation steps, and escalation flow).
- Recommend we codify MSS clamp as a short-term policy in the cutover checklist for on-prem GREs until NGFW fix is verified.

Closing note: system stabilized after changes. Recommend a 48h observation window and then we can remove the MSS clamp if AstraClad confirms the NGFW fix.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
